data.name: AgentNewNamePlaceholder

data.name: AgentBuiltInTip
data.value: This is one of OpenCode's seven built-in agents, so this entry changes shipped behaviour rather than adding a new agent.

data.name: AgentOpaqueNotice
data.value: This entry is not an object, so there is nothing to edit here. It is kept exactly as written and saved unchanged.

data.name: AgentNumberError
data.value: One of the numbers below is not valid. The last good value is kept until it is, so nothing is lost while you type.

data.name: AgentModeTip
data.value: Unset leaves the key out, so OpenCode's own default applies. The other three decide where the agent can be selected.

data.name: AgentColorTip
data.value: A theme role name, or any other string such as a hex value — the schema accepts both, so this list is a suggestion rather than a limit.

data.name: AgentEmptyMeansUnsetTip
data.value: Empty leaves the key out, so whatever this agent would otherwise inherit still applies. Zero is a real setting, not empty.

data.name: AgentTriStateTip
data.value: Three states. Indeterminate leaves the key out, so OpenCode's own default applies — which is not the same as off.

data.name: AgentDeprecatedToolsNotice
data.value: The schema marks this field deprecated — use the permission override instead. It stays editable because removing it would change how this agent behaves.

data.name: AgentAddPermissionTip
data.value: Adds rules that apply on top of the global permission, for this agent only.

data.name: AgentRemovePermissionTip
data.value: Removes the key entirely so this agent inherits the global rules. Different from leaving the override empty, which overrides with nothing.

data.name: CommandOpaqueNotice
data.value: This entry is not an object, so there is nothing to edit here. It is kept exactly as written and saved unchanged.

data.name: CommandInvalidBanner
data.value: command(s) below have no template. The schema requires one, so those entries are invalid — nothing is invented for them.

data.name: CommandShellBanner
data.value: command(s) below run a shell command through the !`...` form. That executes with your privileges every time the command is used, so read them before trusting a config you did not write.

data.name: CommandTemplateTip
data.value: The command body. Supports $ARGUMENTS, positional $1...$n, @file references, and !`cmd` shell interpolation.

data.name: CommandTemplateMissing
data.value: This command has no template. The schema requires one.

data.name: CommandShellWarning
data.value: This template runs a shell command through !`...`. It executes with your privileges whenever the command is invoked.

data.name: CommandSubtaskTip
data.value: Three states. Indeterminate leaves the key out, so OpenCode's own default applies — which is not the same as off.

data.name: PluginOpaqueBanner
data.value: entry(ies) below match neither form the schema allows. They are kept exactly as written and saved unchanged.

data.name: PluginOptionErrorBanner
data.value: entry(ies) below have options that are not valid JSON for an object. The last valid options are kept until they are, so nothing is lost while you type.

data.name: PluginOpaqueNotice
data.value: This entry matches neither a bare specifier nor a [name, options] pair, so there is nothing to edit. It is saved unchanged.

data.name: PluginHasOptionsTip
data.value: Off writes just the specifier. On writes the two-element [name, options] form — which is a different value even when the options are empty. Your options text is kept either way.

data.name: PluginOptionsTip
data.value: The schema types this as an object with no declared fields, so it is edited as JSON. Blank counts as an empty object.

data.name: PluginOptionsError
data.value: Not valid JSON for an object. The last valid options are kept meanwhile.

data.name: PluginEnabledOpaqueTip
data.value: This value is not a boolean, so it cannot be toggled here. It is kept exactly as written.

data.name: PluginEnabledHint
data.value: Toggles plugins that something else declares, so a name here need not appear in the plugin list.

data.name: ToolingModeNotSetHelp
data.value: Writes nothing: the key stays out of this file, so a lower-priority scope decides.

data.name: ToolingModeDisabledHelp
data.value: Writes false. Same effect as leaving the key out, but stated here so a lower-priority scope cannot switch it back on.

data.name: ToolingModeBuiltInsHelp
data.value: Writes true. Built-ins are on, with no per-language overrides.

data.name: ToolingModeConfiguredHelp
data.value: Writes an object: built-ins are on, plus the overrides below. An empty object is valid and is not the same value as true.

data.name: ToolingUnrecognisedBanner
data.value: This value is neither true, false, nor an object, so it is held exactly as written rather than interpreted. Saving changes nothing here until you replace it.

data.name: ToolingReplaceValueTip
data.value: Discard the held value and start from an editable configuration. The held value cannot be recovered afterwards.

data.name: ToolingMoveEarlierTip
data.value: Move earlier. This is argv, so the order is the meaning.

data.name: ToolingMoveLaterTip
data.value: Move later. This is argv, so the order is the meaning.

data.name: FormatterNoEntries
data.value: No per-formatter overrides yet. Built-in formatters still apply.

data.name: FormatterOpaqueBanner

data.name: FormatterOpaqueNotice
data.value: This entry is not an object, so it is held exactly as written.

data.name: FormatterDisabledTip

data.name: FormatterCommandTip
data.value: The command and its arguments, one per row. This is argv, so the order is the meaning.

data.name: FormatterEnvironmentTip

data.name: FormatterExtensionsTip

data.value: entry(ies) below are not objects. They are held exactly as written and saved unchanged.

data.value: This entry is not an object, so it is held exactly as written.

data.name: LspExtrasBanner
data.value: entry(ies) below carry fields this editor does not show. They are preserved, not dropped.

data.name: LspExtrasNoticeFmt
data.value: {0} field(s) not shown here are preserved exactly as written.

data.name: LspIncompleteBanner
data.value: entry(ies) below match neither form the schema allows. An entry needs either a command, or nothing at all but disabled set to true. OpenCode rejects the file until they do.

data.name: LspIncompleteNotice
data.value: This entry matches neither form the schema allows. Add a command, or clear every other field and leave only disabled set to true.

data.name: LspDisabledTip
data.value: Three states. Checked writes disabled: true, unchecked writes disabled: false, and indeterminate leaves the key out. On an entry with no command, only the checked state is valid on its own.

data.name: LspCommandTip
data.value: Required unless the entry says nothing but disabled: true. This is argv, so the order is the meaning.

data.name: LspExtensionsTip
data.value: File extensions this server claims. Order carries no meaning.

data.name: LspEnvTip
data.value: Written under env. A formatter entry uses environment instead; the two keys are not interchangeable.

data.name: LspHasInitializationTip
data.value: Send an initialization object to the server when it starts.

data.name: LspInitializationTip
data.value: The schema declares no fields here, so this is raw JSON. While the text is not a valid object the last valid value is kept, so nothing is lost as you type.

data.name: LspInitializationError
data.value: Not valid JSON for an object. The last valid value is being kept.

data.name: LspInitializationErrorBanner
data.value: entry(ies) below have initialization JSON that is not a valid object. The last valid value is kept until it is, so nothing is lost while you type.

data.name: AutoupdateHint
data.value: How OpenCode handles new releases. Three values, and leaving the key out is a fourth state — a lower-priority scope decides that one.

data.name: AutoupdateNotSetHelp
data.value: Writes nothing: the key stays out of this file, so a lower-priority scope decides.

data.name: AutoupdateDisabledHelp
data.value: Writes false. Same effect as leaving the key out, but stated here so a lower-priority scope cannot switch it back on.

data.name: AutoupdateNotifyHelp
data.value: Writes the string "notify". OpenCode tells you a release exists and installs nothing.

data.name: AutoupdateAutomaticHelp
data.value: Writes true. OpenCode installs new releases without asking.

data.name: AutoupdateUnrecognisedBanner
data.value: This value is neither true, false, nor the string "notify", so it is held exactly as written rather than interpreted. Note that "notify" is case-sensitive.

data.name: AutoupdateReplaceValueTip
data.value: Discard the held value and choose one of the three the schema allows. The held value cannot be recovered afterwards.

data.name: KeybindHint

data.value: {0} action(s) hidden by the current filter.

data.value: ⚠ {0} action(s) name a key another action also names. OpenCode does not state which one wins.

data.value: {0} action(s) here are not in this build's schema. They are kept exactly as written.

data.name: KeybindUnknownAction

data.name: KeybindUnrecognisedBanner
data.value: ⚠ This scope's keybinds value is not an object, so it cannot be edited here. It is held exactly as written and saved unchanged.

data.name: KeybindActionHeldBanner

data.name: KeybindBindingHeldBanner
data.value: ⚠ This binding matches no known form. It is held exactly as written; the others stay editable.

data.name: KeybindReplaceValueTip
data.value: Discard the held value and start from an editable one. What is written now is lost.

data.name: KeybindModeNotSetHelp
data.value: Writes nothing: the action stays out of this file, so a lower-priority scope decides.

data.name: KeybindModeDisabledHelp
data.value: Writes false. The schema admits only false here — there is no true.

data.name: KeybindModeNoneHelp
data.value: Writes the string "none". Same effect as false, and a different file — neither is rewritten into the other.

data.name: KeybindModeBoundHelp
data.value: Writes the binding on its own. Not the same file as a one-item list.

data.name: KeybindModeSequenceHelp
data.value: Writes an array, even when it holds one binding. Not the same file as a bare binding.

data.name: KeybindFormChordHelp
data.value: Writes the text exactly as typed. OpenCode parses it; this editor does not, because the schema states no grammar for it.

data.name: KeybindFormKeyHelp
data.value: Writes { "name": … } with only the modifiers you set. This is the form the schema specifies exactly, so it is what capture produces.

data.name: KeybindFormEventHelp
data.value: Writes { "key": … } plus event, preventDefault and fallthrough. The key inside may itself be typed text or a structured key.

data.name: KeybindCaptureTip
data.value: Press a key and this records it as name plus modifiers. The name is a best-effort spelling — the schema constrains it in no way, so correct it if OpenCode wants another.

data.name: KeybindKeyNameTip
data.value: The schema types this as any string, so no spelling can be validated here. Capture fills in a conventional lowercase name.

data.name: KeybindMetaTip
data.value: The schema's meta. Capture fills this from Alt.

data.name: KeybindSuperTip
data.value: The schema's super. Capture fills this from the Windows or Command key.

data.name: KeybindHyperTip
data.value: No desktop platform reports Hyper, so capture never sets it. Set it by hand if your terminal sends it.

data.name: KeybindStructuredKeyTip
data.value: Untick to state this binding's key as typed text instead of as name plus modifiers. Both are legal here.

data.name: KeybindBindingIncomplete
data.value: ⚠ This binding names no key, which OpenCode rejects. It is still written as typed.

data.name: EssentialsPageSubtitle
data.value: The settings that most change what OpenCode is allowed to do, what it costs, and which file it reads. Everything here is also reachable from its own settings page.

data.name: EssentialsCardAutoupdateBody
data.value: Whether OpenCode replaces its own binary when a release appears. "Notify only" tells you a release exists and installs nothing, which keeps a long session on the version it started with.

data.name: EssentialsCardRulesBody
data.value: The global AGENTS.md OpenCode loads into every session, whichever directory it comes from. Project rules are not shown here — they depend on which project you are in.

data.name: EssentialsRulesNone
data.value: No global AGENTS.md, so OpenCode starts every session with no global rules.

data.name: EssentialsRulesShadowedBanner
data.value: Both your redirected config directory and the default ~/.config/opencode contain an AGENTS.md. OpenCode may be reading only the default one and silently ignoring yours — this is reported upstream and could not be confirmed against the installed version, so treat it as a thing to check rather than a certainty.

data.name: EssentialsCardActiveConfigBody
data.value: Which file this app is editing. OpenCode's own "debug paths" command reports the default directory even when OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR points somewhere else, so this is worth stating plainly.

data.name: EssentialsActiveConfigInline
data.value: OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT is set — OpenCode is reading its configuration from that variable, not from a file.

data.name: EssentialsActiveConfigInlineBanner
data.value: OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT overrides the files. Edits saved here are written to disk but will not change what OpenCode reads until that variable is cleared.
